scenes.heading: Medallion Architecture
scenes.narration: The medallion architecture organizes a lakehouse into three progressively refined layers, Bronze, Silver, and Gold, so data quality improves as it flows toward consumers.

scenes.heading: The three layers
bullets: Bronze holds raw, ingested data as-is
Silver holds cleaned, conformed, deduplicated data
Gold holds business-level aggregates and marts
Each layer is a durable, queryable checkpoint
scenes.narration: The Bronze layer captures raw source data exactly as ingested, preserving history and enabling replay. The Silver layer cleans, validates, deduplicates, and conforms that data into well-typed, joined entities. The Gold layer aggregates Silver data into business-ready tables such as marts, features, and reporting aggregates. Because each layer is materialized and queryable, it acts as a durable checkpoint you can rebuild downstream layers from.

scenes.heading: Data refining through the layers
scenes.narration: Source data first lands in the Bronze layer untouched, which gives you a faithful, replayable record. Transformations then clean and conform it into the Silver layer, applying schema enforcement, deduplication, and joins to build trustworthy entities. From Silver, aggregation and business logic produce Gold tables tailored to specific consumers. Those Gold tables feed BI dashboards, machine-learning features, and executive reports with data whose quality has been raised step by step.

scenes.heading: Bronze vs Gold
scenes.narration: Bronze data is raw and untransformed, so it is high in volume and low in direct usability, but it serves as the immutable source of truth you can always reprocess from. Gold data is curated and aggregated, far smaller in volume and highly usable, and it is shaped and optimized for the queries consumers actually run. The layers in between let you localize changes: fix a cleaning rule in Silver, or a metric definition in Gold, without touching raw ingestion.

scenes.heading: What each layer typically holds
bullets: Bronze: append-only raw with ingestion metadata
Gold: aggregates, marts, and ML features
scenes.narration: In practice, Bronze holds append-only raw records enriched with ingestion metadata like load time and source, so you can always trace and replay. Silver holds well-typed, deduplicated, and conformed business entities, having applied schema enforcement and joins. Gold holds business aggregates, reporting marts, and machine-learning features tailored to consumers. Data quality checks act as gates between layers, so bad records are quarantined rather than silently promoted, which keeps trust high the further along data travels.

scenes.heading: Why the pattern scales teams
bullets: Analysts and ML own Gold definitions
scenes.narration: The medallion layering maps naturally onto team ownership. Ingestion teams own getting raw data reliably into Bronze. Data engineers own the cleaning and conforming logic that builds Silver. Analysts and machine-learning teams own the business definitions and features in Gold. Because each layer exposes a clear contract to the next, teams can evolve their own layer without breaking others, which reduces the cross-team friction that otherwise slows a growing data platform.

scenes.text: Medallion gives every dataset a clear quality contract, so producers, cleaners, and analysts can improve their layer independently.
scenes.narration: The medallion pattern assigns every dataset a clear quality contract by layer, which lets ingestion, cleaning, and analytics teams each improve their own layer independently while consumers always know exactly what guarantees they are getting.
